description: Enterprise IT governance policy based on COBIT 2019 principles for governance of enterprise IT.
content:
# IT Governance Framework Policy

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes the governance framework for enterprise IT based on COBIT 2019 principles.

## 2. Scope
Applies to all IT decisions, investments, and operations across the organization.

## 3. Governance Principles
- Ensure IT delivers value to the business
- Optimize risk management
- Align IT with business strategy
- Manage IT resources responsibly
- Monitor and evaluate IT performance

## 4. Governance Structure
- IT Steering Committee for strategic decisions
- IT Investment Review Board for portfolio management
- Architecture Review Board for technical standards

## 5. Responsibilities
- Board: Ultimate accountability for IT governance
- CIO: Strategic IT leadership
- IT Management: Operational execution

title: Incident Management Policy
description: Establishes procedures for detecting, reporting, and responding to security incidents
content:
This policy establishes incident management requirements per ISO 27001 Annex A.16.

Incident Classification:
- Critical: Business-critical systems affected, data breach suspected
- High: Multiple systems affected, potential data exposure
- Medium: Single system affected, no data exposure
- Low: Minor security events, no business impact

Response Requirements:
1. Incidents must be reported within 1 hour of detection
2. Critical incidents require immediate escalation to CISO
3. Root cause analysis required for all High/Critical incidents
4. Lessons learned documented and shared

title: Industrial Control System Security Policy (IEC 62443)
description: OT/ICS security policy for operational technology environments based on IEC 62443.
content:
# Industrial Control System Security Policy

## 1. Purpose
Secure industrial automation and control systems per IEC 62443 requirements.

## 2. Scope
All operational technology, SCADA, DCS, and industrial control systems.

## 3. Security Levels
- SL 1: Protection against casual or unintentional violations
- SL 2: Protection against intentional violations using simple means
- SL 3: Protection against sophisticated attacks
- SL 4: Protection against state-sponsored attacks

## 4. Zone and Conduit Model
- Define security zones based on criticality
- Implement conduits for cross-zone communication
- Apply appropriate security levels per zone

## 5. Security Requirements
- Access control for all IACS components
- Network segmentation and monitoring
- Patch management for OT systems
- Incident response procedures

title: Information Security Management System (ISMS) Policy
description: Establishes the organization commitment to information security and defines the ISMS scope and objectives
content:
This policy establishes the foundation for our Information Security Management System (ISMS) in accordance with ISO 27001:2022. It defines leadership commitment, scope, objectives, and the framework for managing information security risks across the organization.

Key Requirements:
1. Leadership shall demonstrate commitment to the ISMS
2. Information security objectives shall be established and communicated
3. Resources required for the ISMS shall be determined and provided
4. The ISMS shall be integrated into organizational processes
5. Continual improvement of the ISMS shall be pursued

title: NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls Compliance Policy
description: Policy ensuring compliance with Saudi NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls for all organizational entities.
content:
# NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC) Compliance Policy

## 1. Purpose
Ensure organizational compliance with the National Cybersecurity Authority Essential Cybersecurity Controls.

## 2. Applicability
All entities operating in Saudi Arabia subject to NCA regulations.

## 3. Control Domains
- Cybersecurity Governance
- Cybersecurity Defense
- Cybersecurity Resilience
- Third-Party Cybersecurity
- Cloud Cybersecurity

## 4. Compliance Requirements
- Annual self-assessment against ECC controls
- Remediation of identified gaps
- Reporting to NCA as required
- Periodic external assessments

## 5. Governance
- CISO accountable for ECC compliance
- Regular reporting to executive management
- Board oversight of cybersecurity posture

title: NIS2 Directive Compliance Policy
description: Compliance with EU Network and Information Security Directive 2
content:
This policy establishes compliance requirements per NIS2 Directive.

Essential and Important Entity Requirements:
1. Risk management measures
2. Incident handling and reporting (24-hour notification)
3. Business continuity and crisis management
4. Supply chain security
5. Cybersecurity training for management and staff

Penalties for Non-Compliance:
- Essential entities: Up to €10M or 2% of global turnover
- Important entities: Up to €7M or 1.4% of global turnover

title: NIST CSF Detect Policy
description: Continuous monitoring and anomaly detection per DETECT function
content:
This policy establishes detection requirements per NIST CSF 2.0 DETECT function.

Detection Capabilities:
1. Continuous Security Monitoring
2. Adverse Event Analysis
3. Network Traffic Analysis
4. User Behavior Analytics
5. Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)

Alert Thresholds: Critical alerts require 15-minute response. High alerts require 1-hour response.

title: NIST CSF Governance Policy
description: Establishes cybersecurity governance aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 GOVERN function
content:
This policy establishes cybersecurity governance per NIST CSF 2.0 GOVERN function.

Governance Requirements:
1. Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities defined
2. Board oversight of cybersecurity risk
3. Cybersecurity strategy aligned with business objectives
4. Supply chain risk management integrated
5. Continuous improvement through metrics and KPIs

Organizational Context: Enterprise risk appetite, legal requirements, and stakeholder expectations drive cybersecurity priorities.

title: NIST CSF Identify Policy
description: Asset management, risk assessment, and organizational understanding per IDENTIFY function
content:
This policy establishes identification requirements per NIST CSF 2.0 IDENTIFY function.

Key Areas:
1. Asset Management: Hardware, software, data, systems inventory
2. Business Environment: Mission, objectives, stakeholders, dependencies
3. Governance: Policies, legal, regulatory requirements
4. Risk Assessment: Threat identification, vulnerability assessment
5. Supply Chain Risk: Third-party dependencies and risks

title: NIST CSF Protect Policy
description: Safeguards to ensure delivery of critical services per PROTECT function
content:
This policy establishes protection requirements per NIST CSF 2.0 PROTECT function.

Protection Categories:
1. Identity Management and Access Control
2. Awareness and Training
3. Data Security
4. Platform Security
5. Technology Infrastructure Resilience

Implementation Priority: Protect controls prioritized based on asset criticality and risk assessment.

title: NIST CSF Recover Policy
description: Recovery planning and improvements per RECOVER function
content:
This policy establishes recovery requirements per NIST CSF 2.0 RECOVER function.

Recovery Objectives:
- RTO (Recovery Time Objective): 4 hours for critical systems
- RPO (Recovery Point Objective): 1 hour for critical data
- MTPD (Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption): 24 hours

Recovery Activities:
1. Recovery Plan Execution
2. Improvements based on lessons learned
3. Internal and external communications

title: NIST CSF Respond Policy
description: Response planning and communications per RESPOND function
content:
This policy establishes response requirements per NIST CSF 2.0 RESPOND function.

Response Plan Components:
1. Incident Response Team activation
2. Incident Analysis and forensics
3. Incident Containment strategies
4. Stakeholder Communications
5. Incident Improvements and lessons learned

Communication: Regulatory notifications within 72 hours for data breaches.

title: PCI DSS Cardholder Data Protection Policy
description: Protects cardholder data in accordance with PCI DSS v4.0 requirements
content:
This policy establishes cardholder data protection requirements per PCI DSS v4.0.

Cardholder Data Elements:
- Primary Account Number (PAN) - must be rendered unreadable when stored
- Cardholder Name, Service Code, Expiration Date

Sensitive Authentication Data (never stored after authorization):
- Full track data, CAV2/CVC2/CVV2/CID, PIN/PIN block

Key Requirements:
1. Minimize cardholder data storage
2. Encrypt transmission over open networks
3. Protect stored data using approved cryptography
4. Implement strong access controls
5. Regularly test security systems

title: PCI DSS Network Security Policy
description: Establishes network segmentation and firewall requirements for PCI compliance
content:
This policy establishes network security requirements per PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1.

Network Segmentation:
- CDE (Cardholder Data Environment) isolated from other networks
- All traffic between CDE and external networks through firewall
- DMZ for public-facing systems

Firewall Rules:
1. Deny all traffic by default
2. Only explicitly authorized traffic permitted
3. Rules reviewed every 6 months
4. Changes require documented business justification

title: RBI Cybersecurity Framework Compliance Policy
description: Compliance with Reserve Bank of India cybersecurity guidelines for financial services
content:
This policy establishes compliance requirements per RBI Cybersecurity Framework.

Key RBI Requirements:
1. Board-approved cybersecurity policy
2. Cyber Security Operations Center (C-SOC)
3. Incident reporting to RBI within 6 hours
4. Annual vulnerability assessment and penetration testing
5. Third-party security assessments

IT Risk Management:
- Risk assessment methodology aligned with RBI guidelines
- Business continuity plan with 4-hour RTO for critical systems
- DR site in geographically separate location

title: Risk Assessment and Treatment Policy
description: Defines the methodology for identifying, analyzing, and treating information security risks
content:
This policy establishes the risk assessment and treatment process aligned with ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2.

Risk Assessment Process:
1. Identify assets and their owners
2. Identify threats and vulnerabilities
3. Assess likelihood and impact using 5x5 matrix
4. Calculate risk score and prioritize treatment
5. Document risk treatment decisions and acceptance criteria

Risk Treatment Options: Modify, Retain, Avoid, or Share risks based on organizational risk appetite.

title: SAMA Cybersecurity Framework Policy
description: Compliance with Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority cybersecurity framework
content:
This policy establishes compliance requirements per SAMA Cybersecurity Framework.

SAMA CSF Domains:
1. Cyber Security Leadership and Governance
2. Cyber Security Risk Management and Compliance
3. Cyber Security Operations and Technology
4. Third Party Cyber Security

Key Requirements:
- Board oversight of cybersecurity
- CISO reporting to Board/CEO
- Annual penetration testing
- Quarterly vulnerability assessments
- 24x7 SOC operations

title: SEBI Cybersecurity Circular Compliance Policy
description: Compliance with SEBI cybersecurity requirements for market intermediaries
content:
This policy establishes compliance requirements per SEBI Cybersecurity Circular.

SEBI Requirements for Market Intermediaries:
1. Mandatory cyber security audit annually
2. System audit by CERT-IN empaneled auditor
3. Two-factor authentication for trading
4. Incident reporting to SEBI and exchanges

Data Protection:
- Client data encrypted at rest and in transit
- Data localization within India
- Retention as per SEBI regulations (5-8 years)

title: UAE NESA Information Assurance Standards Policy
description: Policy for compliance with UAE National Electronic Security Authority standards for critical infrastructure.
content:
# UAE NESA Information Assurance Standards Policy

## 1. Purpose
Ensure compliance with UAE National Electronic Security Authority information assurance requirements.

## 2. Scope
All critical national infrastructure entities and government-related organizations.

## 3. Security Requirements
- Information security management system
- Asset management and classification
- Access control and authentication
- Network and communications security
- Incident management and response

## 4. Compliance Approach
- Align with NESA IAS requirements
- Conduct periodic security assessments
- Implement remediation plans
- Report to relevant authorities

## 5. Accountability
- Senior management oversight
- CISO implementation responsibility
- Regular compliance reporting
